model_config.endpoint_verified: 2026-08-19 live 200 OK (account REDACTED-AWS-ACCOUNT, us-east-1, scoped key)
model_config._budget_note: Client-side HARD cap, enforced per call before sending. AWS has no native Bedrock spend cap and AWS Budgets lags billing data by hours. Sized from baseline_kimi.json: the reserved run costs ~$31 on Terra / ~$3 on Qwen3 at measured token volumes, with worst case ~$77 on Terra if every call saturated the 4096 ceiling. Raise deliberately, never silently.
model_config._provenance: Values marked PENDING_PROBE or null are deliberately unset. probe_bedrock.py resolves them from measurement; do not fill them in by hand. AWS docs state structured outputs and count-tokens are NOT supported for this model on bedrock-runtime, so structured_output stays false and the frozen v0.5.1 decoding mode is retained without amendment.
model_config._version_pin_note: NO VERSION PIN IS AVAILABLE FOR THIS MODEL. Verified live on 2026-08-19: the response echoes model="global.openai.gpt-5.6-terra" (the alias itself, not a resolved underlying version) and system_fingerprint=null. There is also no dated variant of the id in list-foundation-models. So neither of the two pinning routes works: the config cannot pin it and the response does not reveal it. This is a LIMITATION TO DECLARE in the protocol annex, not something to engineer around: if AWS moves the model behind the alias mid-run, the data will not show it. Mitigations available: (a) record the run window start/end timestamps so the served version is at least bounded in time, (b) keep the Qwen3 arm, whose weights are public, as the reproducible anchor.

_response_shape_verified.note: Reasoning tokens are counted and billed but the reasoning TEXT is not returned in message.content. Expected consequence for extraction: no think markers in content, so the frozen policy parses the whole message. Probe P5 confirms on a real payload.

_measured_2026_08_19.A2_response_format: ACCEPTED_AND_JSON with {"type":"json_object"}. NOTE: the AWS model card states structured outputs are unsupported on bedrock-runtime; JSON mode evidently is supported. Full json_schema mode is NOT yet tested. Enabling it would change the frozen decoding mode -> Renxi decision.
_measured_2026_08_19.determinism: NONE. temperature=0 -> HTTP 400 ("Only the default (1) value is supported"). top_p=1 accepted (it is the default). seed ACCEPTED BUT NOT HONOURED: three identical calls with seed=13082642 produced three different outputs (92/66/107 output tokens, three distinct hashes). The frozen v0.5.1 determinism clause cannot be satisfied on this arm in any form.
_measured_2026_08_19.output_ceiling: max_completion_tokens works; max_tokens returns HTTP 400 'unsupported_parameter'. Rejected, not silently ignored - the safe failure.
_measured_2026_08_19.extraction: No think markers in content. The frozen extraction policy parses the whole message and returned COMPLETED_VALID with ZERO schema errors on a real dev call. extraction_policy.json needs NO change for this arm.
_measured_2026_08_19.reasoning_effort: low/medium/high all accepted. Completion tokens on one real dev call: low=76 (reasoning 0), medium=116 (reasoning 47), high=108 (reasoning 38). Non-monotonic at n=1 - cannot pick a level from this; needs a dev sweep.
_measured_2026_08_19.token_efficiency_vs_kimi: ~110 output tokens vs Kimi mean 1495 (see baseline_kimi.json). About 13x more efficient. Truncation risk at the frozen 4096 ceiling is effectively zero, versus 4.0% on Kimi.
